meta.name: qu.et — Editorial Luxury Reference DNA
meta.description: Scale, spacing, typography, composition and motion DNA extracted from 4 references. Color/palette intentionally excluded — qu.et uses a fixed dark greige palette.

color.palette_type: out-of-scope — qu.et fixed dark greige palette, not derived from references
color.contrast_strategy: all 4 refs use near-monochrome, high-contrast single-hue sections (black-on-white, white-on-black, or single saturated block) rather than multi-tone palettes — confirms dark-greige-only approach is consistent with this genre

display.weight: 400–800 (ranges from thin serif italic to black grotesk)

font_families.heading: serif editorial italic (Tom Wood hero, Charlotte Chesnais wordmark) paired with condensed/grotesk bold display (ORE, x21 wordmark)
font_families.body: neutral grotesk sans, small size, generous line-height

typography.font_style_notes: two-voice system: a quiet serif-italic for intimate/editorial moments (hero captions, taglines) vs. an oversized bold grotesk for scale-statement moments (hero word, footer wordmark). The jump between body (14px) and display (200px+) is the core signature — no mid-scale filler.

spacing.content_density: spacious — large sections of pure negative space between image blocks and type blocks
spacing.section_rhythm: full-viewport-height sections (100vh hero, 100vh+ product close-up) alternate with short breather sections (~200–300px) of centered caption text, then another full-bleed block

layout.grid_system: 12-col desktop grid, but content treated in large asymmetric blocks rather than evenly distributed columns
layout.max_content_width: 1440px container; imagery and wordmarks break out to 100vw edge-to-edge
layout.gutter: 0–4px between paired full-bleed images; 24–32px between text/content blocks
layout.alignment_tendency: mixed — centered for hero captions, strict edge-to-edge for imagery and wordmarks, left-aligned for product info panels

shape.border_usage: none to subtle 1px hairline dividers between footer columns
shape.divider_style: thin 1px hairline, full-width or column-width, low-contrast

elevation.shadow_style: none — flat editorial surfaces, depth comes from photography not shadow
elevation.depth_cues: scale contrast and cropping, not shadow/blur

iconography.style: minimal line icons (search, bag, menu, arrow)

motion.easing: ease-out, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) feel — confident decelerate, no bounce
motion.entrance_pattern: fade-up with slight scale (0.98→1) on scroll into view; wordmark/hero text often slides in from mask-reveal
motion.exit_pattern: simple fade-out, no dramatic exit choreography
motion.philosophy: minimal, cinematic restraint — motion exists to reveal scale, not to decorate

components.button_style: ghost text link with small arrow, uppercase tracked label, no visible border in default state
components.card_style: borderless image cards with caption below-left in small uppercase tracked type
components.navigation_pattern: minimal top bar: logo centered or left, hamburger + search + account icons right, no visible nav links on homepage
components.modal_style: flat white/cream panel, no rounding, hairline close icon top-right
components.list_style: footer nav as uppercase label + plain-weight link list, 3–4 column groups
components.component_notes: CTAs are typographic, not boxed — relies on underline/arrow rather than button chrome

aesthetic.visual_metaphor: fashion editorial spread / art book, not e-commerce grid

visual_language.ornamentation: none — the only ornament is scale contrast in type
visual_language.whitespace_usage: primary compositional tool; used to isolate single statements
visual_language.visual_weight_distribution: extreme — either near-empty or a single dominant full-bleed element, no even distribution
visual_language.focal_strategy: single hero element per section, strict one-idea-per-viewport
visual_language.contrast_level: high (image vs. void, giant type vs. tiny caption)
visual_language.texture_usage: skin/fabric/material close-ups carry all texture; no applied UI texture

composition.hierarchy_method: scale contrast between massive type/image and minuscule caption text
composition.flow_direction: vertical scroll narrative, each section a discrete 'page'
composition.grouping_strategy: paired images (2-up) separated by hairline gutter; isolated hero elements get full section to themselves
composition.negative_space_role: active compositional element, not filler — used to slow pacing and signal luxury

imagery.photo_treatment: tight crop, natural/editorial lighting, skin and material tone close-ups
imagery.graphic_elements: none beyond type and hairline rules
imagery.image_shape: full-bleed rectangle, no rounding, occasional square crop for product detail

interaction_feel.hover_behavior: image micro-zoom (1.0→1.03) or caption underline reveal

brand_voice_in_ui.formality: formal-casual hybrid, like a fashion magazine caption
brand_voice_in_ui.cta_style: subtle suggestion — small arrow link, never a loud button

overview.primary_technology: CSS + scroll-triggered JS (IntersectionObserver / GSAP ScrollTrigger class libraries typical of this genre)

text_effects.type: clip-reveal on giant display type (ORE example reveals word via mask as section enters)
text_effects.description: large display words slide/mask into view once per section
text_effects.technology: CSS clip-path or GSAP SplitText-class reveal

image_effects.description: subtle scale-up on image hover for product cards

visual_effects.composite_notes: Effects are intentionally restrained across all 4 refs — the 'wow' factor comes from typographic scale and full-bleed photography, not from JS-driven effects. The only recurring motion signature is the mask/clip reveal on oversized type (ORE hero word, x21 giant wordmark footer) paired with simple scroll-fade on everything else.

qu_et_application_rules.rule: Hero section = full 100vh, single full-bleed image/scene, no copy block competing for space. Caption text (collection name) centered, 24–32px serif italic, positioned at 35–45vh from top — not dead-center, slightly upper-middle like tomwood-home.
One 'giant typography' story section per page (homepage and/or about): a single word or short phrase set at 14–18vw, line-height 0.85, bleeding to the container edges, mask-reveal on scroll-in.
qu_et_application_rules.px_vw: font-size: clamp(80px, 16vw, 280px); line-height: 0.85; horizontal padding: 24px mobile / 48px desktop

qu_et_application_rules.rule: Product page: single dominant close-up image occupies ~70% of first viewport height, info panel (title/price/details) constrained to a narrow column (max 360px) positioned top-right, small serif italic title at 20–24px.
qu_et_application_rules.px_vw: hero image height: 70vh; info column max-width: 360px; title size: 20–24px

qu_et_application_rules.rule: Below the hero product image, drop to a 2-up image grid with a 2–4px hairline gutter (not 24px) — pairing feels intentional/tight, unlike generic e-commerce grids.
Section-to-section rhythm: alternate full-bleed visual blocks (100vh) with short text-breather sections capped at 240–320px height, copy centered, max-width 640px, 14–16px body.
qu_et_application_rules.px_vw: breather section height: 240–320px; copy max-width: 640px; body size: 14–16px

qu_et_application_rules.rule: Footer wordmark: brand name set in giant weight spanning near-full container width, sitting below standard footer nav columns — treat as its own closing 'statement' section, not inline with nav.
qu_et_application_rules.px_vw: wordmark font-size: clamp(100px, 22vw, 420px); top margin from nav block: 64–96px; horizontal edge padding: 24px

qu_et_application_rules.rule: Footer nav columns: 3–4 groups, uppercase tracked labels 10–11px with 0.08–0.12em letter-spacing, link list 13–14px regular weight, 8px vertical rhythm between links.
qu_et_application_rules.px_vw: label size: 10–11px, tracking 0.1em; link size: 13–14px; link spacing: 8px

qu_et_application_rules.rule: Image captions under product/collection images: small, bottom-left aligned over or just below image, 10–11px uppercase tracked, paired with a small arrow for 'view' affordance — never a boxed button.
qu_et_application_rules.px_vw: caption size: 10–11px; offset from image edge: 16–24px

qu_et_application_rules.rule: Hover interaction budget is small: image scale(1.02–1.03) over 500–600ms ease-out on product/collection cards; caption underline reveal on text links. No parallax beyond 10–20% speed differential on hero background.

Negative space before major reveals (giant type, footer wordmark) should be a full empty/near-empty section (min 200px, often full 100vh) — never crowd a scale-statement element directly against other content.
